chunks: That I may do some good I did not do (in the world)." Not so. These are only words he utters. Behind them lies the intervening barrier (stretching) to the day of their resurrection.

key_terms.بَرْزَخٌ: The intermediate realm or barrier between death and resurrection

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Barzakh in the context of Surah Al-Mu'minun?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the finality of death as a 'Barzakh' (isthmus) where the soul is sealed, rendering the regret of 'I wish I had done good' ineffective as a means of redemption. It underscores the concept of *al-Kalimah al-Muqarrarah* (the decisive word), indicating that the utterance itself becomes a binding testimony against the individual in the intermediate realm. This reinforces the Shia emphasis on seizing opportunities for righteous deeds before the soul reaches the grave, where the window for repentance closes.
